body:
U5 shipped on branch cursor/u5-belt-board-one-read-dbdf. Parts 2 and 3 are in: CHAMPIONS spends G15 BeltLineage for every entry's reign strip and a new board line over the scope. Full suite 164/164, rankings_hub_panel_test 87/87.

PART 1 IS NOT TAKEN and needs your call. get_championships_read() is FOUR TIMES SLOWER than the eight singular calls it was meant to replace: 520ms against 129ms on the seeded save, reproduced three times. It builds contenders for every belt in the WORLD (57 on that save, eight disciplines) when the board draws 8 in one discipline x sex. get_championships() under it is 0.3ms and 8x get_division_rankings() is 2.9ms, so the entire cost is career.duplicate(true) - 58 copies against 16. Neither read's contenders are ever drawn by this board. The fix is in GameState (one snapshot, contenders only for the keys asked for), which U5 forbids me to touch. Once it lands, part 1 is a one-line swap in rebuild().

TWO ENGINE FACTS THE BOARD WAS PRINTING WRONG, both fixed on the panel side: (1) a world-seeded belt stores since_week 0 (WorldPopulation.gd:1035), so the board printed SINCE WEEK 0 on every seeded belt - the common case, not an edge; (2) when a belt changes hands the engine stamps last_defended_week with the WIN week and defenses 0 (WorldPopulation.gd:1294-1298), so a brand-new champion read as 0 DEFENCES with a defence date. The count is now the fact: no defences means NEVER DEFENDED whatever the date says.

G15 NEEDS ONE LINE: BeltLineage.reign() was briefed title_status 'held', but the engine writes 'champion' (WorldPopulation.gd:11) and ChampionshipRead passes it through, so every real champion comes back state 'unknown'. I translated at the panel seam rather than edit Grok's file - belt_lineage_test locks 'held' and G15 still reads OPEN. Worth accepting both words in the module.

Also: board() ranks any row with a recorded since_week, and _vacate_on_the_scale keeps since_week, so it will name a VACANT belt the longest or newest reign. The panel guards it; any other consumer of board() must too.
